R1073.decision_summary: R1073 §5.39 §5.16 §5.35 PR-27.4 multi-window key dispatch close-during-dispatch fix: R1071's live-focus gate left a blind spot that survived into sprag's live GUI — a toggle-class shortcut whose FIRST dispatch closes the OS-focused window (sprag dock) moves OS focus to the successor window, so a stray re-delivery of the SAME physical press to that NOW-focused window passed is_key_dispatch_window and fired a second time (dock->undock bounce; one physical press, two dispatches 32ms apart, REPEAT=false, trigger=window close). R1071 only dropped a stray to the now-UNFOCUSED source window. Fix = press-time focus snapshot: ShellCore.key_press_owner pins, at each press's admitted rising edge, the window the press began on; ShellCore::admit_key_press is the single gate both the live KeyboardInput arm and the key_press_for_window seam consult — a continuation press (auto-repeat or stray re-delivery) is admitted only at its OWNER window AND while that window still holds OS focus, so the conjunction catches the now-unfocused-source stray (R1071, fails focus half) and the now-focused-successor stray (R1073, fails owner half) with one rule. Owner released on the keyup (note_key_state pressed=false, window-agnostic), never on blur, so the gate is robust to either winit focus-event ordering on the close-driven handoff. admit_key_press is strictly additive over R1071 (all 4 R1071 tests unchanged); single-window byte-identical.
changes_bullets: ShellCore.key_press_owner: HashMap<key string -> window> — per-key press-time OS-focus snapshot pinned at each physical press's admitted rising edge; out-of-band shell state alongside os_focused_window (mirrors a winit/OS fact the key event does not carry, never scene data, §2 #7 unaffected)

ShellCore::admit_key_press(window,key) — the single dispatch-admission gate both the live GUI and the seam consult: rising edge (no owner) admits iff is_key_dispatch_window (fail-open) and pins owner=window; continuation (owner present — auto-repeat or stray re-delivery) admits iff owner==window AND is_key_dispatch_window(window). The conjunction drops a stray re-delivery to the now-UNFOCUSED source window (R1071's case, fails the focus half) OR to the now-FOCUSED successor window (R1073's blind spot, fails the owner half) with one rule
ShellCore::key_press_for_window now routes through admit_key_press (was is_key_dispatch_window alone), so the per-window key seam gains the press-owner snapshot

ShellCore::note_key_state clears the key's owner on the release edge (pressed=false), window-agnostic so a keyup delivered to the successor window still clears an owner whose source window the dispatch closed; NOT cleared on blur / clear_held_keys, so the gate is robust to either winit focus-event ordering on the close-driven handoff

AppShell live WindowEvent::KeyboardInput routes presses through the SAME admit_key_press (single source of truth with the seam), the canonical W3C key string resolved once; arm body extracted to handle_keyboard_input to keep window_event under the clippy::too_many_lines (100) ceiling (the app.rs split convention shared with handle_mouse_button / handle_file_dnd)

R1071's four tests survive unchanged (held_toggle auto-repeat-fires-once / stray-to-unfocused-source gated / single-window byte-unchanged / note_os_focus either-event-ordering) — admit_key_press is strictly additive over the live-focus gate (continuation = owner-half AND focus-half conjunction), so neither gate relaxes

STRUCTURE SURVIVED: crate-home ShellCore is correct (OS-focus-handoff is GUI-only — TUI is single-OS-window — so this is the one case R882.1's policy-in-CoreShell does NOT apply); RPC/a11y bypass of admit_key_press is correct (gate models an OS re-delivery RPC cannot create); release-clear-not-blur is load-bearing. CLEARED genuine defects: (HIGH) Escape/Tab are dispatched by handle_key_press (Escape->exit/modal-cancel, Tab->traverse) yet took the gate's None branch (R1071 focus-gate only, no owner snapshot) and the doc falsely claimed admit_key_press was the single SSOT for ALL keys -> new dispatch_named_key_str gate vocabulary (a superset of the R1009 content/chord named_key_str adding the 2 shell-reserved keys), chord_key/gate_key split, owner lifecycle moved to a dedicated ShellCore::note_key_release (reverted from note_key_state so the RPC-exposed held_names chord subset stays unpolluted); (MED) remove_window did not reconcile os_focused_window so a destroyed focused window left a stale Some(dead) that failed the gate CLOSED for every live window (swallow-all-input) -> remove_window clears it (fail-open), key_press_owner deliberately NOT cleared there (would re-open the successor stray); (NIT) per-keystroke spec_id.to_owned on the auto-repeat hot path -> handle_keyboard_input takes Copy WindowId + recomputes spec_id; (NIT) round-stamped test module renamed multi_window_key_dispatch_gate. Deferred to R1074: surface os_focused_window + press-owner via §7 RPC introspection (north-star AI-first).
changes_bullets: HIGH (SSOT reviewer): Escape/Tab are dispatched by handle_key_press (Escape->exit/modal-cancel, Tab->traverse) but took the gate's None branch (R1071 focus-gate only, no owner snapshot), and the doc falsely claimed admit_key_press is the single source of truth for ALL keys. Fix: new app::dispatch_named_key_str = the gate's DISPATCH vocabulary, a superset of the R1009 content/chord named_key_str that adds the two shell-reserved dispatched keys Escape/Tab; handle_keyboard_input resolves chord_key (chord cache, named_key_str, UNCHANGED) and gate_key (owner gate, dispatch_named_key_str) in one match, so EVERY key handle_key_press dispatches is owner-gated, not just chord keys; the live None branch now covers only non-dispatched keys (gate result moot) -> admit_key_press is genuinely the one gate for all dispatched keys

owner lifecycle decoupled from the chord cache: new ShellCore::note_key_release (the release peer of admit_key_press) clears the press-owner; note_key_state reverted to the pure R1071 chord-cache funnel, so covering Escape/Tab in the gate does not pollute the RPC-exposed CoreShell::held_names chord subset (named_key_str / HeldKeys stay the ratified narrow vocabulary)

MED (north-star reviewer): remove_window now reconciles os_focused_window (clears it if it names the window being torn down) so a destroyed focused window fails the gate OPEN (fail-safe default) not CLOSED (a stale Some(dead) made is_key_dispatch_window false for every live window = swallow-all-input). key_press_owner is deliberately NOT reconciled in remove_window: an in-flight press whose own dispatch closed the window is exactly the stray to drop, so its owner must survive the close and self-clear on the keyup; clearing it on destruction would re-open the now-focused-successor stray

R1083.decision_summary: R1083 §5.51 §5.45 §5.16 tabbed docking: add an ADDITIVE DockNode::Tabs { id, panels, active } tab-well variant (>=2 invariant + collapse-to-Leaf at 1 = no dual representation; existing Leaf/Split serde+matches stay byte-identical) with a stable well id mirroring Split's; new DockTopology::tabify(source,target,new_tabs_id) primitive (remove source, stack onto target: Leaf->2-tab well / existing well->append+activate); route DockDropZone::Center -> DockReorganizeIntent::Tabify through the intent_for_zone SSOT (supersedes the tab-less v1 Swap) so the already-wired R1081/R1082 pointer + invoke coordinators tabify live for free; remove/split/swap recursions + the validator made well-aware (new TopologyError TabsTooFew/ActiveOutOfRange/DuplicateTabsId); render the well as a view_tabs strip keyed on the well id above the active panel rendered header-suppressed (DockPanelStyle::show_header) so a drop resolves the active panel id (edge->split whole well, centre->tabify); view_tabs tag lifted &'static str -> impl Into<Cow> (2nd consumer). Click-to-switch-active / tab-reorder / untab-drag-out / dock-well tab a11y are DECLARED-DEFER (R1084+, each its own forcing consumer).
changes_bullets: Model: add DockNode::Tabs { id, panels: Vec<panel_id>, active } as an ADDITIVE variant (existing Leaf/Split serde + match arms + tests stay byte-identical) — the tab well. Invariants enforced by DockTopology::try_new: panels.len() >= 2 (a single-panel well is a Leaf, never a degenerate Tabs), active < panels.len(), every panel id + the well's own stable id unique-and-non-empty in the one topology id namespace. The well carries a stable id mirroring Split's stable-id rationale (binds the view_tabs strip tag + future per-well selection signal).

Counts/walks: collect_panel_ids descends a well (all panels, tab order); new panel_count() (Leaf=1 / Tabs=len / Split=sum) = panel_ids().len(); leaf_count counts a well as one pane slot; split_count unchanged (Tabs=0). DockNode::tabs() constructor + DockTopology::panel_count() delegator.

Validation: NodeKind::Tabs + insert_panel_id helper shared by the Leaf and Tabs arms (a panel id collides identically whether in a leaf or a well). New TopologyError: DuplicateTabsId, TabsTooFew, ActiveOutOfRange; well-id-vs-panel/split collision => IdCollision; panel-in-well duplicating a leaf => DuplicatePanelId.

Mutation: remove_leaf_rec well-aware — shrink a well, clamp active, collapse to Leaf at 1 panel (the canonical >=2 rule, no dual representation); split_leaf_rec well-aware — an edge drop onto a panel inside a well splits the WHOLE well (stays together as one Split child); swap_panel_ids_rec relabels panels inside wells; NEW DockTopology::tabify(source, target, new_tabs_id) = remove source then stack onto target (Leaf -> 2-tab well / existing well -> append + activate); source==target is a no-op.

Routing (SSOT): intent_for_zone Center => DockReorganizeIntent::Tabify (supersedes the tab-less v1 Swap; Swap stays a valid public mutation but no zone produces it). DockReorganizeIntent::Tabify { source, target } + source()/target()/apply() arms; apply()'s new_split_id generalized to new_id (split id OR fresh well id). DockReorganizer gains a tabs_seq counter + tabs_seq() accessor; apply_intent mints reorg-tabs-{seq} for Tabify (REORG_TABS_ID_PREFIX) and bumps only the counter the applied gesture drew from. The already-wired R1081/R1082 pointer + invoke coordinators tabify live for free (no new pointer wiring).

Render: view_dock_surface_node Tabs arm renders a view_tabs strip (keyed on the well id) above the active panel's content; the active panel uses view_dock_panel with the header suppressed (DockPanelStyle::show_header, default true) — the strip is the title row — keeping its drop_target root + content + drop overlay so a drop onto the well resolves the active panel id (edge => split the whole well, centre => tabify into it). Substrate lift: view_tabs tag generalized &'static str -> impl Into<Cow<'static, str>> (2nd consumer = dock wells with runtime-minted ids forces it; hello-tabs unchanged).

Consumer: hello-dock-panels-editor external-capacity hint uses panel_count() (counts well panels individually). 21 R1083 unit tests (tabify model / well shrink-collapse / split-a-well / 5 validation rejections / panel_ids+counts / swap-in-well / Center=>Tabify SSOT / apply_intent mints reorg-tabs-0 + bumps only tabs_seq / walker strip+active-content+header-suppression / Tabs serde round-trip).

DECLARED-DEFER (R1084+, each its own forcing consumer): live click-to-switch active tab (per-well selection External + signal), tab reorder within a strip (R742 on tab composite tags), untab-by-drag-out gesture, dock-well tab a11y roles (tablist/tab/tabpanel).

Core: DockReorganizer holds Rc<Signal<Option<DockTopology>>> (was non-Option). new()/topology() take/return the Option signal. apply_intent: `let Some(current) = topology.get() else { record "empty surface — no-op"; return Ok(..) }` — the empty surface is the IDENTITY no-op (no source to drag, no target to drop), the honest total definition, not defensive code; on Some it is the existing path and sets Some(next). with_undo records SignalEdit<Option<DockTopology>> (next = Some). DockReorganizeExternal::new takes the Option signal; query("topology") serialises None -> JSON null (AI reads the empty dock as null, not a fabricated tree).

Why total not weakened-topology: DockTopology keeps its leaf>=1 invariant (try_new/panel_ids/walker/serde all stand on it); absence is modelled by the Option, never by a degenerate empty topology. The coordinator provably never emits Some->None: Swap/SplitInsert/Tabify all preserve panel count (moves), remove_leaf on the sole leaf is RootRemoval error not None — so None is input-only, and a pointer drag cannot even originate on an empty surface (only the invoke path reaches it, and it gets the no-op).

R1084.1.decision_summary: R1084.1 §5.51 §5.45 §5.16 adversarial audit-clearance of R1083 (tabbed docking) + R1084 (reorganize-over-Option): 3 read-only reviewers (craft+honesty / SSOT+structure / north-star+AI-introspection) + author grep/read re-verification. STRUCTURE SURVIVED — every major decision affirmed (additive DockNode::Tabs = genuine model addition with a distinct stable well id + one canonical form per panel count enforced on every path, NOT dual-modeling; Option-unify > parallel new_optional+TopologyHandle; intent_for_zone = sole zone->intent across all 4 drive paths; view_tabs Cow lift + show_header + dual counters justified; clean model/routing/render layering) and the core logic re-confirmed correct. Cleared: (1) the one reachable code defect the author under-flagged — same-well tabify silently re-minted the stable well id (RPC reorganize naming an inactive well member ran the collapse-then-re-promote path); new activate_in_shared_well makes a same-well drop an in-place activation preserving the id + order, else the cross-pane relocate path; (2) tabify source==target no-op now routes through try_new (single-construction-path uniformity); (3) stale docs (resolve_dock_drop + DockReorganizeIntent enum/Swap-variant + swap_leaves all said centre=Swap / 'leaf' / two-variants; R1084 Option-lift residue across 4 doc sites) corrected; (4) misleading r686_external_invoke_center_swaps test (passed coincidentally, distinguished nothing) renamed + asserts the 'type':'Tabs' structural distinction; (5) AI-first symmetry — tabs_seq added to the External schema + query (was split_seq-only); (6) reserve-hint +2 NIT. Honesty sharpened: tab wells are create+observe+AI-activate-via-reorganize; explicit activate_tab verb + pointer click-to-switch + tab a11y are R1085 and click-to-switch is load-bearing for navigability (not a peer of reorder/untab). 7574 pass / 0 fail.
changes_bullets: Adversarial audit-clearance of R1083 (tabbed docking) + R1084 (reorganize-over-Option): 3 read-only reviewers (craft+honesty / SSOT+structure / north-star+AI-introspection) in parallel + author grep/read re-verification. STRUCTURE SURVIVED — every major design decision affirmed adversarially; the reviewers + author re-derivation independently confirmed the core logic correct (remove_leaf_rec active-index math, .expect()/unreachable! reachability, None-totality, additive-Leaf byte-identical, split-a-well, panel_count/leaf_count coherence). The clearance fixes one reachable code edge + stale docs + one false test + an introspection-symmetry gap + honesty framing.

CODE DEFECT (MED, the one the author under-flagged): same-well tabify silently re-minted the stable well id. tabify(source,target) only guarded source==target, not "both already in one well". For a 2-panel well [b,c], an RPC reorganize{source:"c",target:"b",zone:Center} ran the remove+restack path: remove c -> [b] collapses to Leaf{b} -> re-promoted under a FRESH new_tabs_id, discarding the well id the binding's per-well state keys on. Reachable via the AI primary path (an AI names an inactive well member; a pointer drag can only grab the visible tab). Fix: new `activate_in_shared_well(node,source,target)` — if both are in the SAME Tabs well, rebuild with that well's active = source's index (preserving id + panel order = in-place activation), else None -> the cross-pane remove+restack path. tabify checks it before the relocate path. Incidentally this gives the AI a navigation primitive (reorganize an inactive tab onto a well-mate = activate it). 3 tests (same-well 2-panel + larger-well preserve id/order/activate; cross-pane still relocates + mints fresh id = guard is narrow).

CRAFT #5 (LOW): tabify source==target no-op constructed DockTopology directly, bypassing try_new (inconsistent with swap_leaves which routes through try_new "to keep the single-construction-path invariant uniform"). Fixed -> Self::try_new(self.root.clone()).

STALE DOCS (craft+SSOT, MED/LOW, the repo's anti-stale-doc discipline): (a) resolve_dock_drop "centre hit produces Swap" -> Tabify; (b) DockReorganizeIntent enum doc "two variants / tab-less v1 / centre=Swap" + the Swap variant's own "centre drop" -> rewritten to three variants, centre=Tabify, Swap = valid mutation NO zone produces; (c) swap_leaves doc "two named leaves / no leaf / This is the Center gesture = swap" -> "panels", "no panel", "no zone produces a swap (R1083 made centre tabify); swap_leaves is the explicit-swap primitive", + note it relabels panels inside wells; (d) R1084 Option-lift residue: R686 mutation-header + DockReorganizer.undo field doc + editor external_set_is_dynamic comment + pinion-core widget_core.rs doc example all said Signal<DockTopology> / SignalEdit<DockTopology> -> Option-corrected.

MISLEADING TEST (craft #3, MED): r686_external_invoke_center_swaps_topology_signal sent zone:Center, commented "swapped topology", asserted panel_ids==[b,a,c] — passed coincidentally (tabify of a-onto-b in Split(a,Split(b,c)) yields Split(Tabs[b,a],c), panel_ids also [b,a,c]), distinguishing NOTHING. Renamed r1083_external_invoke_center_tabifies_topology_signal + asserts the topology JSON contains "type":"Tabs" (a swap would be all Leaves) — a real regression net against silent Center->Swap reversion.

AI-FIRST SYMMETRY (north-star #2, LOW/MED): DockReorganizeExternal schema()/query() advertised split_seq but not tabs_seq. Added ("tabs_seq","int") to schema + a "tabs_seq" query arm (mirrors split_seq) so an AI auto-discovering capabilities sees tab-well-mint progress as a first-class observable. Test: schema lists it + query returns 0 then 1 after a tabify.
NIT: editor reserve hint dropped the +2 for the unconditional reorganize+undo anchors — restored.

AFFIRMED (reviewer verdicts, not changed): additive DockNode::Tabs is a genuine model addition (distinct stable well id, not dual-modeling; >=2 + collapse-to-Leaf = one canonical form per panel count, enforced on every path); Option unify > parallel new_optional+TopologyHandle (the enum would be a 2nd source of truth for the topology handle); intent_for_zone = sole zone->intent across all 4 drive paths (no bypass); view_tabs &'static str->Cow lift driven by the real dock 2nd consumer; show_header justified (1 consumer, default-true byte-identical); dual split_seq/tabs_seq counters justified (distinct prefixes); well-id != panel-id addressing; clean model/routing/render layering.

HONESTY FRAMING SHARPENED (north-star/craft Finding 6): the tab well is create + observe + (post-fix) AI-activate-via-reorganize, but explicit activate_tab verb + pointer click-to-switch + tab reorder + untab + dock-well tab a11y roles remain R1085 — and click-to-switch/activation is LOAD-BEARING for navigability (not a peer of reorder/untab as R1083 framed it). The editor registers a DockPanelExternal per panel incl. inactive (unpainted) tabs; harmless (inert until the panel is activated, and the dynamic external set re-runs on topology change) but noted.

R1085.decision_summary: R1085 §5.51 §5.45 §5.16 tab-well navigation slice (a) — the AI-first activate_tab primary. R1083's DockNode::Tabs wells were create+observe-only; this makes them navigable by RPC/AI over the existing SSOT, in three layers. (1) DockTopology::set_active_tab(well_id, index): a pure topology primitive — NOT a move (no panel relocates, no id minted, only the well's active changes) — returning a new validated topology; set_active_in_well_rec rebuilds the matching well (mirrors activate_in_shared_well); a stale/wrong-kind id -> new TopologyError::TabsWellNotFound, an out-of-range index -> try_new's existing ActiveOutOfRange (the one validation gate, not re-checked in the primitive). (2) DockReorganizer: extracted apply_intent's last_outcome + undo-or-set tail into a private commit() funnel — now the sole-writer SSOT both gestures pass through (the R1082.1 invariant preserved, not broken by a second writer) — and activate_tab navigates over it: empty surface = identity no-op, rejection self-records 'rejected:', success commits, bumping neither split_seq nor tabs_seq (navigation mints no id). (3) DockReorganizeExternal: invoke('activate_tab',{well_id,index}) arm + ('activate_tab','json') schema entry + thin delegate — the third action shape beside drop/reorganize, discoverable so an AI switches tabs symbolically (no pixels), the §2 #2 RPC-as-primary-path contract. Scope is slice (a) only: pointer click-to-switch (R1086) + dock-well tab a11y (R1087) share this same coordinator and follow. 7587 pass / 0 fail; committed locally, NOT pushed.

R1086.decision_summary: R1086 §5.21 §5.16 PR-30 (sprag R68 consumer-forced seam): view_splitter's flex children could not set a main-axis min:0, so a panel whose content is larger than its ratio share clamped to content and overflowed — the sprag P2 drag-to-dock symptom (a vertical split put both panels at full window height, the second off the 600px window). Root cause (source-verified): LayoutStyle had no min_size field; flex_basis:0 (R684) alone is the incomplete half of the CSS proportional-flex idiom — without min-*:0 taffy's automatic flex minimum pins each item to its content's min-content size. Fix, audit-first over the existing flex_basis substrate: (1) LayoutStyle gains pub min_size: Size + with_min_size builder + Hash inclusion; default Size::auto() lowers to taffy min_size: Auto = the pre-R1086 automatic minimum, so every binding's layout AND the §5.16 paint-fragment cache key stay bit-identical. (2) to_taffy_style lowers min_size per axis via to_dimension (analogous to size); a SizeValue::Px(0) axis overrides the automatic minimum to zero so a flex child can shrink below its content. (3) view_splitter::apply_flex_main (threaded with orientation) zeroes the MAIN-axis min (Horizontal->width, Vertical->height) on its ratio children, cross axis left Auto so AlignItems::Stretch still fills it; the 7 Scene arms refactored through a set_flex_main helper so flex_basis:0 + flex_grow + min:0 are set uniformly. Verification: a layout.rs regression witness proves the bug (no min override -> 800px content clamp -> second panel off-screen at y>=600) AND the fix (min:0 -> 0.5 ratio = ~300 each, both on-screen); a view_splitter end-to-end forcing-consumer mirrors sprag's vertical_reorganize_keeps_both_panels_onscreen guard (both panels on-screen, handle keeps thickness, panels+handle fill the viewport). 7595 pass / 0 fail. sprag consumes in a sprag-native session (pin bump only, no sprag code change expected; R60 fill_definite Percent(100) is orthogonal to min:0). Committed locally, NOT pushed.

Default `Size::auto()` lowers to taffy `min_size: Auto` = the CSS automatic flex minimum = the pre-R1086 behaviour, so every existing binding's layout AND the §5.16 paint-fragment cache key stay bit-identical.

R1087.decision_summary: R1087 §5.16 §5.41 §2 #7 PR-31 foundation (sprag R68 handoff): the floating-panel-as-positioned-window substrate for dock tear-off. Architecture DECIDED = A — model the floating panel as a real window whose position is declared SSOT data, the drag writes that position to the signal, the shell reconciles; B/C (borderless follower / in-app ghost) are NOT forks but render fallbacks BELOW the contract (dual-representation + AI-invisible = the §2 #2/#7 smell A avoids). This round lands the de-risked, fallback-compatible substrate; the live drag-follow coordinator + libXtst set_outer_position-under-grab acceptance are R1088 (HW-gated). (1) WindowSpec gains pub position: Option<(i32,i32)> (logical px, the doc-predicted additive field) + with_position builder + #[serde(default)] (legacy Signal<Vec<WindowSpec>> JSON omitting it -> None, never a breaking serde change); default None = WM placement = byte-identical for every pre-R1087 binding. (2) resume_spec honours position at create via WindowAttributes::with_position. (3) reconcile_windows gains a move pass — a pure window_position_moves(old,new) diff (unit-testable, no event loop) + Window::set_outer_position apply — keeping reconcile TOTAL over the new field (the R1084 totality lesson: the id-keyed add/drop passes would otherwise silently swallow a same-id position change the top-level new==old guard already saw). (4) scene/windows read-only RPC (pinion_rpc::DeclaredWindow {id,title,position} via DispatchContext::with_declared_windows, resolved shell-side by declared_window_specs from windows_signal else the static windows(), gated on the method) makes the position observable as scene-as-data — the §2 #7 obligation for the new state and the exact justification for choosing A over the AI-invisible follower/ghost. Forcing consumer: hello-dock-panels tear-off pushes a positioned floating WindowSpec (per-panel cascade offset). Verified: 6 move-diff unit tests + 1 WindowSpec position serde/default test + 3 scene/windows handler tests + r1087 RPC demo (26 asserts) tearing off and reading positions back over scene/windows; cargo test --workspace green / clippy clean / fmt clean / validate-workspace T1=0. Honest: headless + unit only — live OS placement and drag-to-follow are R1088 (HW-gated); the foundation is architecture-A-correct AND follower-fallback-compatible, so it does not bet on the live grab-move. Committed locally, NOT pushed.
changes_bullets: WindowSpec gains `pub position: Option<(i32,i32)>` (logical-px outer position, the doc-predicted additive field on the #[non_exhaustive] struct) + a `with_position(x,y)` builder + `#[serde(default)]` so a Signal<Vec<WindowSpec>> value serialized before the field existed deserializes to None — additive, never a breaking change to the reactive primitive's serde shape. Default None = window-manager placement = byte-identical for every pre-R1087 binding.

resume_spec (AppShell) honours a declared position at window-create time via WindowAttributes::with_position (the non-cached creation path); the cached suspend/resume path is untouched (a window keeps its OS position across resume).

reconcile_windows gains a move pass: a pure window_position_moves(old,new) -> Vec<(id,(x,y))> diff (a same-id spec whose declared position changed, including None->Some first-placement; a Some->None drop-back is deliberately NOT a move since set_outer_position has no hand-back-to-WM form) + a Window::set_outer_position apply over the live WindowSlot. This keeps reconcile_windows TOTAL over the new field — without it the id-keyed add/drop passes silently swallow a same-id position change the top-level new==old guard already detected (the R1084 totality lesson).

scene/windows read-only RPC: pinion_rpc::DeclaredWindow {id,title,position} wire type + DispatchContext::with_declared_windows + handle_scene_windows (HandlerKind::Read; None -> DeclaredWindowsUnavailable, the PacingStateUnavailable honesty parity; empty Vec is a real value). Shell-side declared_window_specs() (sibling of declared_window_ids) maps each WindowSpec the binding declares — windows_signal when opted in, else the compile-time windows() list, so the read is honest for single-window bindings too — and is resolved only for the scene/windows method (every other dispatch pays nothing). Makes the position observable as scene-as-data (§2 #7) — the exact justification for choosing architecture A over the AI-invisible follower/ghost.

Forcing consumer: hello-dock-panels tear-off now pushes a positioned floating WindowSpec via floating_window_position (a per-panel cascade offset, base (120,90) + step*40) — the first with_position consumer, proving the binding -> windows_signal -> reconcile_windows -> real-window arc.
verification_bullets: 6 pure window_position_moves unit tests (no event loop): unchanged->no moves, same-id position change, None->Some first placement, add-with-position is NOT a move (resume_spec places it), Some->None drop-back is NOT a move, multiple simultaneous moves reported in new order.

1 WindowSpec serde test: with_position round-trips Some((x,y)); the default builder is None; legacy JSON omitting the position key deserializes to None via #[serde(default)] (derived by stripping the key from a current serialize, robust to SizeStrategy's JSON shape).
3 scene/windows handler tests: None -> DeclaredWindowsUnavailable; a declared set serializes id+title+position ([x,y] / null); an empty Vec is a real empty list distinct from the unavailable error.

r1087_dock_window_position.py RPC demo (26 static asserts; the 3-assert _windows helper executes ~20x): boot reports a single WM-placed main (position null); tear-off adds a torn-inspector entry whose declared position is the binding cascade offset; a 3-panel cascade reports 3 distinct well-formed [x,y] positions with main staying null; positions match floating_window_position deterministically; dock-back drops the entry; return to the single-main baseline. Tear-off driven by the tear_off invoke toggle (gesture-free + deterministic; a drag-to-centre now hits PR-29's reorganize/Tabify zone), since R1087 verifies the POSITION the reducer writes, not the gesture.
Gates: cargo test --workspace green (0 fail); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello clean (-D pedantic); cargo fmt clean; mnemosyne validate-workspace T1=0.

Honesty: headless / scene-data + unit assertions only. The LIVE OS placement and drag-to-follow (each pointer move writing the position signal) are NOT verified here — that is the R1088 slice, with libXtst set_outer_position-under-grab acceptance HW-gated on a real-GPU host (the PR-29 owed-live-acceptance precedent). The foundation is architecture-A-correct AND follower-fallback-compatible, so it does not bet on the live grab-move working.

R1092.decision_summary: Completed the scene/windows window-GEOMETRY introspection surface by adding a declared SIZE alongside R1087's declared position: an AI introspecting a multi-window / docked editor layout now reads not merely WHERE each declared window sits but HOW BIG it is declared to be. Sourced from the binding's SizeStrategy SSOT via a new SizeStrategy::declared_size() projection — Fixed/OpenResizable declare an exact open size, IntrinsicAfterFirstPaint declares null (its eventual size is the post-first-paint content bbox, known only as a transient min floor at declare time) — the same null-means-system-determined honesty position uses for a WM-placed window. AUDIT-FIRST PIVOT: the SEED named R1089/R1092 region work; param-schema (the named rpc/methods next slice) was audited and DEFERRED because param shapes live per-handler with no uniform source signature to cross-check (a drift-prone hand-curated registry or a ~73-handler struct-extraction campaign, no forcing consumer yet); window-size is the clean, buildable, headless-demoable AI-first slice that closes the R1087 position-only geometry debt before the next round pivots to the Phase B DCC campaign.
changes_bullets: SizeStrategy::declared_size(self) -> Option<(u32,u32)> added to pinion-shell as the SSOT for "did the binding declare an open size": Fixed{w,h}=>Some, OpenResizable{size,..}=>Some, IntrinsicAfterFirstPaint=>None. Deliberately DISTINCT from initial_logical_size (the literal creation pixels, which returns Intrinsic's min): declared_size answers "what size did the binding DECLARE", and an Intrinsic window declares none — reporting its transient min floor would mislead an AI into reading it as the final geometry.

DeclaredWindow (pinion-rpc, the scene/windows wire payload) gained declared_size: Option<(u32,u32)>, mirroring the position field's declared-not-live, None=system-determined contract; doc rewritten as "declared geometry" (position [R1087] + declared_size [R1092], each null when that axis is system-determined).
Shell declared_window_specs maps declared_size: spec.strategy.declared_size() at the single production construction site; rustdoc updated to "declared geometry".

3rd-consumer self-grep: SizeStrategy now has three match-self projections (initial_logical_size / min_inner_floor / declared_size) but they return semantically distinct values (creation pixels / OS floor / declared size) — idiomatic enum projections, NOT mechanical duplication, no false-unification lift; DeclaredWindow has exactly one production construction site.

R1092.1.decision_summary: LIVE VERIFICATION finding (0 LOC, no round): the R1088 carry "live OS Moved / set_outer_position-under-grab NOT verified headlessly (HW-gated)" is CLEARED for the platform-feasibility question it gated. On re-checking the actual environment (the dev box HAS a real :0 Xorg + gnome-shell/mutter + GPU + libXtst, contradicting the earlier "environment can't" framing), a throwaway ctypes(libX11/libXtst)+xwininfo probe drove the EXISTING scene/window_move over a real visible hello-dock-panels floating window and read the actual OS geometry. Result: mutter honors set_outer_position to the pixel, INCLUDING during an active pointer grab. Conclusion: live dock tear-off drag-follow is PLATFORM-FEASIBLE on mutter; no follower-window fallback needed; only the coordinator code + winit CursorMoved-during-grab delivery remain (buildable, R1080-R1085 pattern). No production code changed; the probe is a scratchpad throwaway (not committed).
changes_bullets: No production code change (0 LOC). This entry records a live-verification finding against the existing R1087/R1088 window-position substrate, run via a throwaway ctypes+xwininfo probe (scratchpad, not committed per the no-temp-test-files rule).
verification_bullets: Probe drove scene/window_move over a REAL visible hello-dock-panels floating window on :0 (Xorg + gnome-shell/mutter, real GPU, scale 1.0); OS geometry read via xwininfo. (1) Plain move: RPC-commanded logical delta == observed OS physical delta to the pixel ((520,260)=>(520,260)); constant +37px Y = gnome title-bar decoration, cancels in the delta. (2) Under an ACTIVE pointer grab, cross-checked two independent ways that AGREE pixel-exact: (2a) XGrabPointer active grab held by the probe -> commanded (510,290) == OS (510,290); (2b) real synthesized button-1 hold over the main window (winit implicit grab, zero physical motion -> no app-drag/WM-move trips) -> commanded (-260,-180) == OS (-260,-180). So a pointer grab does NOT block ConfigureWindow for a different window on this WM. Probe safety: try/finally always released the button + ungrabbed + restored the cursor; no stray process; X auto-releases grabs on client exit (a post-completion XCloseDisplay/use-after-close segfault was cosmetic, after all results printed + cursor restored).
carry_forward_bullets: Still HW-gated (genuinely): the winit CursorMoved-during-grab -> set_outer_position DELIVERY path (the full live coordinator running, not an RPC-injected move) is still only verifiable by a human-observed live drag; that is the coordinator round's acceptance, not a platform unknown anymore.

The coordinator itself (threshold detach -> per-move reposition -> redock/cancel) + the additive drag-API contract extension exposing the absolute cursor remain to be BUILT (buildable + unit-testable headlessly, R1080-R1085 pattern); R1093 default is still the Phase B DCC campaign unless the tear-off coordinator is explicitly prioritized.

LESSON: when a carry says "HW-gated / can't verify", re-check the ACTUAL environment before repeating the label — a real :0 display was present all along; the true constraint was consent-to-occupy-the-live-desktop + non-deterministic visual verification, not impossibility. A 50-line ctypes+xwininfo delta probe closed the platform unknown deterministically.

R1093.decision_summary: Began the live dock tear-off coordinator (PR-31 Tier 3, the sprag-forced handoff) by landing its foundational seam: the §5.15 input-forwarding ENRICHMENT that hands a drag source the absolute window-logical cursor, and exposes the live drag cursor as scene-as-data. The handoff doc's gap #1 was "the absolute cursor never reaches the drag source" — drag_to forwards only the rect-relative DropPoint, which goes None the instant the cursor escapes every tagged region (exactly the tear-off case), so a follow-the-cursor coordinator had no pointer to read. R1092.1 already live-verified the platform half (mutter honors set_outer_position under an active grab), so this round builds the data half. AUDIT-FIRST SCOPE: correct cursor-anchored window PLACEMENT additionally needs the source-window outer position (gap (b), shell-owned) — a second seam — so this round is the clean, complete, headlessly-verifiable foundation (cursor forwarding + AI-introspectable drag cursor); the placement+follow coordinator consuming it is R1094.
changes_bullets: pinion-core External trait: additive drag_to_at(payload,over,cursor:(f64,f64)) + drag_release_at, defaults DELEGATE to the cursor-less drag_to/drag_release so every pre-R1093 source is bit-identical and no source receives both calls. §5.15 input-forwarding ENRICHED not broken (additive default-delegating method, not a breaking drag_to signature change); the begin_drag contract doc corrected to name drag_to_at/drag_release_at as the forward path.

pinion-runtime InputRouter: update_drag forwards drag_to_at(payload,over,(x,y)); the pointer_up release site forwards drag_release_at with the cursor from self.cursors (falls back to drag_release when no cursor recorded). The absolute cursor is forwarded EVEN when the resolved DropPoint is None (cursor off every tag) — the whole point.

pinion-widget-paint DockPanelExternal: new drag_cursor: Cell<Option<(f64,f64)>>; drag_to_at/drag_release_at record it then delegate to the existing drag_to/drag_release (escape/dock/snap-back logic unchanged); reset on begin_drag; persists post-release for observability. Exposed read-only as query("drag_cursor") = [x,y]/null (schema + query + intervene ReadOnly + Debug). drag_cursor_introspect helper sibling of drop_preview_introspect.

3rd-consumer self-grep: the _at seam has one forcing consumer (dock drag_cursor); file_browser/reorder use the cursor-less hooks unchanged via default delegation (no _at need yet). drop_preview_introspect + drag_cursor_introspect are NOT identical (Signal vs Cell) so no lift.
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace 7632 pass / 0 fail; +3 tests (pinion-core drag_at_methods_default_delegate_to_cursorless; pinion-runtime r1093_router_forwards_absolute_cursor_to_drag_source incl. the over=None escape case; pinion-widget-paint r1093_drag_cursor_records_forwarded_cursor_and_resets_per_gesture).

No regression: r742_dnd + r743_tab_reorder (drag consumers via default delegation) PASS. r683_dock_tear_off FAILS identically on clean HEAD (pre-existing headless floating-window-addressability limitation, CI-verified per the SEED) — NOT a R1093 regression (verified by git stash A/B test).
carry_forward_bullets: R1094 = the live tear-off COORDINATOR consuming this seam: threshold early-detach -> per-move set_outer_position follow -> drop-empty=float / drop-zone=redock / cancel=restore. It additionally needs gap (b): the SOURCE-WINDOW outer position to convert the window-logical drag cursor to a desktop position (shell-owned; the drag cursor this round is in the source window frame, not desktop coords). The platform half is already live-verified (R1092.1: mutter honors set_outer_position under an active grab). Architecture A: follow = write WindowSpec.position -> shell reconciles, so most of the coordinator is headlessly verifiable at the windows_signal level.
sprag consumes via pin bump: the drag cursor is now available to a DockPanelExternal subclass / coordinator; the early-detach + redock signals to the binding are the R1094 contract additions.
The mid-drag (per-move) drag_to_at forwarding is unit-verified (atomic scene/drag cannot observe between move and release); the demo verifies the release-point cursor end-to-end.

R1092.1 already live-verified the platform half (mutter honors set_outer_position under an active grab), so this round builds the data half. AUDIT-FIRST SCOPE: correct cursor-anchored window PLACEMENT additionally needs the source-window outer position (gap (b), shell-owned) — a second seam — so this round is the clean, complete, headlessly-verifiable foundation (cursor forwarding + AI-introspectable drag cursor); the placement+follow coordinator consuming it is R1094.
publishable_changes_bullets: pinion-core External trait: additive drag_to_at(payload,over,cursor:(f64,f64)) + drag_release_at, defaults DELEGATE to the cursor-less drag_to/drag_release so every pre-R1093 source is bit-identical and no source receives both calls. §5.15 input-forwarding ENRICHED not broken (additive default-delegating method, not a breaking drag_to signature change); the begin_drag contract doc corrected to name drag_to_at/drag_release_at as the forward path.

pinion-runtime InputRouter: update_drag forwards drag_to_at(payload,over,(x,y)); the pointer_up release site forwards drag_release_at with the cursor from self.cursors (falls back to drag_release when no cursor recorded). The absolute cursor is forwarded EVEN when the resolved DropPoint is None (cursor off every tag) — the whole point.

pinion-widget-paint DockPanelExternal: new drag_cursor: Cell<Option<(f64,f64)>>; drag_to_at/drag_release_at record it then delegate to the existing drag_to/drag_release (escape/dock/snap-back logic unchanged); reset on begin_drag; persists post-release for observability. Exposed read-only as query("drag_cursor") = [x,y]/null (schema + query + intervene ReadOnly + Debug). drag_cursor_introspect helper sibling of drop_preview_introspect.

3rd-consumer self-grep: the _at seam has one forcing consumer (dock drag_cursor); file_browser/reorder use the cursor-less hooks unchanged via default delegation (no _at need yet). drop_preview_introspect + drag_cursor_introspect are NOT identical (Signal vs Cell) so no lift.
publishable_verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace 7632 pass / 0 fail; +3 tests (pinion-core drag_at_methods_default_delegate_to_cursorless; pinion-runtime r1093_router_forwards_absolute_cursor_to_drag_source incl. the over=None escape case; pinion-widget-paint r1093_drag_cursor_records_forwarded_cursor_and_resets_per_gesture).
clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello clean (fixed an as-i64 truncation in the test stub by formatting the f64 directly); cargo fmt clean.

tools/demos/r1093_drag_cursor.py >=30 assertions across A-E PASS: drag_cursor null at boot for all 3 panels, a drag to a point inside the inspector rect (self-drop -> snap-back, NOT tear-off) sets drag_cursor to that exact [x,y] while the panel stays docked, a second in-rect drag tracks the new point, the property panel drag updates only its own slot (per-panel independence), and intervene on drag_cursor is rejected (read-only).

No regression: r742_dnd + r743_tab_reorder (drag consumers via default delegation) PASS. r683_dock_tear_off FAILS identically on clean HEAD (pre-existing headless floating-window-addressability limitation, CI-verified per the SEED) — NOT a R1093 regression (verified by git stash A/B test).
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: R1094 = the live tear-off COORDINATOR consuming this seam: threshold early-detach -> per-move set_outer_position follow -> drop-empty=float / drop-zone=redock / cancel=restore. It additionally needs gap (b): the SOURCE-WINDOW outer position to convert the window-logical drag cursor to a desktop position (shell-owned; the drag cursor this round is in the source window frame, not desktop coords). The platform half is already live-verified (R1092.1: mutter honors set_outer_position under an active grab). Architecture A: follow = write WindowSpec.position -> shell reconciles, so most of the coordinator is headlessly verifiable at the windows_signal level.
sprag consumes via pin bump: the drag cursor is now available to a DockPanelExternal subclass / coordinator; the early-detach + redock signals to the binding are the R1094 contract additions.
The mid-drag (per-move) drag_to_at forwarding is unit-verified (atomic scene/drag cannot observe between move and release); the demo verifies the release-point cursor end-to-end.

changes_bullets: M1 (MUST-FIX, dock.rs): the cursor-less `drag_release` escape-arm now reads `last_source_window` (recorded each `drag_to_at`/`drag_release_at`) instead of hard-coding None — the FINAL release-follow carries the gesture's source window (R1107 fixed only the per-move arm; a floater re-drag's RELEASE re-positioned at main's origin = the R1095.1 defect on the release path). + a dock test that fails without the fix.

S2 (pinion-runtime): `ensure_window` made STRUCTURAL via a `router_for(routers, window_id)` helper used at all ~11 router-access sites — R1107 stamped at only 2 dispatch chokes and silently missed `touch_event_for_window`, so a touch-driven tear-off got source=None→main. Now every per-window dispatch (incl. touch + pointer_down) stamps the window id.

S1 (SSOT, pinion-shell): lifted `desktop_position_from` (config-free, byte-identical across flat+editor, sprag's 3rd copy already drifted) + `window_exists` to pinion-shell (WindowSpec's crate = the only viable home; widget-paint has no shell dep). Both dock consumers now delegate; None falls back to `pinion_runtime::DEFAULT_WINDOW` (dedups the "main" literal). Config-bearing helpers (follow/toggle/redock_panel_floating) correctly stay binding-local. + pinion-shell unit tests.

S3 (test): editor `apply_zone_redock` `# Errors` contract test — a `tear_off_redock_at` whose target names no panel rejects the relocate (topology UNCHANGED) yet still removes the window (panel home, not lost/floating).

N1/N3 (NIT): DragUpdate::source_window doc names the population asymmetry (over_window=transient session vs source_window=router identity); the r1105 redock test targets its OWN slot (home no-op) so it no longer silently triggers an unasserted tabify.

R1108.decision_summary: PR-34 redock-totality DECLINED and the spike (4740ea62+58933736) reverted to e340d97b on framework-first grounds. Making SplitInsert and tabify total over source-presence overloads a move primitive to fabricate a panel, violating pinion's own AI-first name-reference invariant (a move verb referencing a panel by name must reject a bad or stale name, not materialise a ghost) and SRP; the unguarded drop verb proved the regression empirically. The consumer-forced premise was also stale: sprag adopted the R72 placeholder model (the leaf survives a float; sprag's own code states the placeholder model moots PINION-PR34), so no live consumer is leaf-removing and the materialise half served nobody. Strict restored -- both drop and reorganize reject an absent source uniformly, no per-verb guard, no new public surface. A future genuine leaf-removing consumer gets materialisation via a distinct explicitly-named redock primitive, never a move-verb overload.

R630.decision_summary: feat(core): R630 §5.50 from_css_string modern rgb + hsl coverage
changes_bullets: crates/pinion-core/src/style.rs: extend `Color::from_rgb_function` with W3C CSS Color 4 §8.1 modern space syntax (`rgb(R G B)` / `rgb(R G B / A)`) alongside the existing legacy comma form; the entry point now dispatches on comma presence (`body.contains(',')`) to one of two sibling helpers (`parse_rgb_legacy_body` / `parse_rgb_modern_body`), each calling a shared `parse_rgb_channel_triplet` so the percent/integer homogeneity rule stays in one place

crates/pinion-core/src/style.rs: `rgba()` and `rgb()` are now true synonyms per CSS Color 4 §8.1 — both accept 3-channel (no alpha) and 4-channel (alpha) legacy forms; pre-R630 the prefix constrained arity, but the spec says they are interchangeable; updated the R624 arity test accordingly and added R630 tests pinning each synonym path

crates/pinion-core/src/style.rs: add `Color::from_hsl_function(&str) -> Option<Self>` sibling to `from_rgb_function`; supports modern space form (`hsl(H S% L%)` / `hsl(H S% L% / A)`) and legacy comma form (`hsl(H, S%, L%)` / `hsla(H, S%, L%, A)`) with the same dispatch-on-comma pattern; alpha is positional in legacy and `/`-introduced in modern

crates/pinion-core/src/style.rs: add helper free functions `parse_modern_alpha` (number-or-percent), `parse_hue` (degrees with optional `deg`/`rad`/`turn`/`grad` unit, wraps via `rem_euclid` per CSS Values 4), `parse_unit_percentage` (mandatory `%` suffix per CSS Color 4), `hsl_to_srgb_bytes` (W3C §6.2 canonical conversion with achromatic + lightness-extreme short-circuits), and `hue_to_rgb` (W3C piecewise hue-segment helper); CSS-spec canonical short names `h`/`s`/`l`/`r`/`g`/`b`/`p`/`q`/`t` mirror the algorithm letter-for-letter and ride single fn-level `clippy::many_single_char_names` allow attributes with `reason = "CSS Color 4 §6.2 canonical ..."`

crates/pinion-core/src/style.rs: `parse_hue` strip-suffix order — `grad` / `turn` BEFORE `rad` / `deg` because `grad` ends with `rad`; a naive longest-first miss would false-positive (`"100grad".strip_suffix("rad") = Some("100g")` → parse fails); documented in source comment

crates/pinion-core/src/style.rs: `Color::from_css_string` dispatcher gains a third arm for `hsl(`/`hsla(`; the doc-comment is updated with the R630 support matrix (modern rgb space + slash alpha + hsl); deferred forms reduce to `oklch()` / `lab()` / `color()` (Level 4 wide-gamut) and named colors

crates/pinion-core/src/style.rs: append 27 R630 unit tests covering modern integer/percent triplets / slash-alpha number + percent / multi-whitespace tolerance / wrong-arity reject / out-of-range alpha reject / HSL primaries (red/green/blue) / modern + legacy hsl forms / achromatic short-circuit / lightness extremes / hue wrap (720° ≡ 0°, -360° ≡ 0°) / all four hue units (deg/rad/turn/grad) / unknown unit reject / bare S/L reject / out-of-range percent reject / wrong-arity reject / missing-parens reject / dispatcher arms; 2 R630 sibling tests pin the rgb/rgba synonym contract; 1 R624 test reworded to reflect the spec-canonical (rgb∧rgba == synonyms) arity rule

R634.decision_summary: feat(cli): R634 §5.7 pinion figma-verify sub-command + Figma REST fetch
changes_bullets: Cargo.toml: add `clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive"] }` and `ureq = { version = "2", features = ["json", "tls"], default-features = false }` to `[workspace.dependencies]`; ureq runs sync at the CLI boundary (no tokio runtime) and uses rustls for portable TLS without a native OpenSSL link
crates/pinion-cli/Cargo.toml: add the new deps + a `[[bin]] name = "pinion"` block so the binary is invoked as `cargo run -p pinion-cli -- ...` (or `pinion ...` once installed)

crates/pinion-cli/src/main.rs: replace the pre-R634 `fn main() {}` stub with a `clap` derive root (`Cli` + `Command` enum) routing to the first sub-command `figma-verify`; future sub-commands land alongside the round that needs them per the [[abstraction-needs-second-consumer]] discipline

crates/pinion-cli/src/figma_verify.rs: new module — `FigmaVerifyArgs` (file_key positional + `--output` + `--ids` flags) and `run(&FigmaVerifyArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>>` that reads `FIGMA_TOKEN` env var, calls the Figma REST `GET /v1/files/:key` endpoint with optional `?ids=` filter, deserializes to `serde_json::Value`, pretty-prints, and writes to stdout or the `--output` path

Figma authentication contract: token is sourced exclusively from `FIGMA_TOKEN` env var — the CLI never reads from a config file or accepts the token as a flag, so accidental shell-history / git-blame leakage is impossible by construction; the recommended scope is `File content` read-only (figma.com → Settings → Personal access tokens)

Wire shape: `FILE_KEY` is the URL path segment between `/design/` (or `/file/`) and the file name in a Figma URL; the response is the full DocumentNode tree (FRAME / GROUP / RECTANGLE / TEXT / VECTOR / etc. all typed) which R635 will map to `Scene` / `LayoutStyle` / `BoxStyle`

R636.decision_summary: feat(cli): R636 §5.7 pinion figma-fetch-image sub-command + Figma reference PNG verified
changes_bullets: crates/pinion-cli/src/figma_image.rs: new module — `FigmaImageArgs` (file_key + node_id positional + `--output` required + `--scale` (default 1.0) + `--format` (default png)) and `run(&FigmaImageArgs)` that implements the documented two-leg Figma image fetch: (1) `GET /v1/images/:key?ids=:node&format=:format&scale=:scale` returns a per-node S3 URL map, (2) `GET <s3_url>` returns the actual binary PNG bytes; pre-signed URL needs no auth header

crates/pinion-cli/src/main.rs: register the new `figma-fetch-image` sub-command under the `Command` enum + dispatch in `main` next to the R634 `figma-verify` arm; `mod figma_image;` declared above the existing `mod figma_verify;`

Figma response error surfacing — the image-list endpoint reports per-call failures in a top-level `err` JSON field; the CLI propagates the message verbatim so a node-id typo or invisible-node error reaches the user with the exact Figma wording (vs being swallowed under a generic HTTP 200)

First real-world fetch — `cargo run -p pinion-cli --release -- figma-fetch-image qluPDRsuDuPM3deySb0ejR '51553:5180' --output /tmp/figma-btn-ref.png --scale 2` produced a 2946-byte 218×80 RGBA PNG (109×40 native size at scale=2); the image confirms the Material 3 Filled Button visual: fully-rounded purple pill, white `Button` label centered, white leading `+` Material Symbols icon — the trailing-icon slot exists but is empty in this particular variant rendering

Reference image inspection identified the first substrate-gap evidence: the Figma rendering includes a Material Symbols `+` glyph in the leading-icon slot that the R635 hand-write elided to a placeholder (Figma `INSTANCE` node referencing an external glyph component). The pinion-side rendering will visibly differ at the leading-icon position once R635 paint output is captured — first concrete design-parity gap landed in the audit queue

cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello → clean

End-to-end fetch → 218×80 RGBA PNG written to /tmp/figma-btn-ref.png; `file` reports `PNG image data, 218 x 80, 8-bit/color RGBA, non-interlaced` — exact size at scale=2 confirms the dimension contract (109×40 native × 2)

Visual inspection via Read tool surfaces the Material 3 Filled Button: rounded pill, M3 Primary color matching the #675AA4 spec, `Button` label, leading `+` glyph; consistent with the R634-extracted spec at node `51553:5180`

carry_forward_bullets: R637 §5.7 — pinion-side screenshot capture: `cargo run --release -p figma-button-m3` (or a headless smoke harness) → `scene/screenshot` RPC PNG export at 109×40 native + 218×80 retina, then a pixel-diff against `/tmp/figma-btn-ref.png` with a similarity score; needs to handle the dimension match (pinion shell defaults to 320×160 canvas, the button sits inside — either crop pinion output to the button rect via `scene/bbox` lookup, or pad the Figma reference)

R637+ §5.7 substrate gap (FIRST EVIDENCE landed): Material Symbols icon glyph system. Figma renders the leading `+` from an external Material Symbols font; pinion has no icon-font substrate so the leading-icon slot is currently empty in the R635 binding. Three textbook-canonical options: (a) bundle a Material Symbols subset as a SVG path table, (b) treat Material Symbols as a regular `pinion-text` font and let parley shape the glyph by codepoint, (c) new `pinion-icons` crate with a typed `Icon` enum mapping name → SVG path data. (b) is the smallest delta to existing substrate; defer the architectural pick to R638 once a second Figma binding with icons evidences the same need (Cards / Chips / FABs all use Material Symbols)

R637+ §5.50 substrate gap: pixel-diff library choice — `image` + `imageproc` crates are the canonical Rust pair (image decodes PNG, imageproc has SSIM / per-channel diff). Alternative is to vendor a minimal `pixelmatch`-style algorithm so pinion-cli stays light. Decide once R637 lands the screenshot side

R649.decision_summary: R649 §5.23 R27 — Effect side-effect suppression during dry_run/simulate via SimulationGuard thread-local; non-idempotent Effect chains stay idempotent across hypothetical-mutation cycles
changes_bullets: pinion-core/src/reactive/simulation.rs (new): IS_SIMULATING thread-local Cell<bool> + SimulationGuard RAII (Drop restores prior; nesting-safe). is_simulating() query. 3 unit tests pin baseline + flip-on-enter + nested-guard semantics.

pinion-core/src/reactive/effect.rs: Effect::mark_dirty checks is_simulating() between in_run/cancelled checks and weak-self upgrade. Suppresses Effect closure body during simulate scopes; subscription set unaffected (frozen at last rerun), so next post-simulation Signal::set fires the Effect normally.
pinion-core/src/reactive/mod.rs + lib.rs: re-export SimulationGuard + is_simulating at the public surface so pinion-rpc (and future binding-internal dry_run consumers) can compose.
pinion-rpc/src/dry_run.rs: wrap dry_run() body in SimulationGuard::enter(). Single-write External rollback now reactive-safe — no Effect side-effect lands twice.

pinion-rpc/src/simulate.rs: simulate() + simulate_with_owner() both enter SimulationGuard. Nested guard is fine (simulate_with_owner enters first, simulate's inner enter sees prior=true). Owner.restore inside the same scope so Signal value writes during restore don't fire Effects either.

pinion-rpc/src/simulate.rs: new r649_effect_suppressed_during_simulate test — naive `Effect: counter.set(counter.get()+1)` pattern (the R647-era set_with workaround target) is now correct under R649: simulate_with_owner leaves counter at pre-call value, proving R26+R27 compose to give full idempotency.

carry_forward_bullets: R650 candidate: isolated Computed cache (§5.30 R30). Computed values cached during simulate may pollute live cache. Less critical than R27 (cache eviction is benign mostly) but spec commitment open.

Not urgent — surface only if a binding hits this debug case.

changes_bullets: examples/todomvc/src/main.rs: TodoFilterExternal (~199 LOC bespoke handler) retired; framework RadioGroupExternal(3) registered under FILTER_TAG with seeded selection. FilterRadioStates struct added to Self::State tuple ((TextFieldState, u32, FilterRadioStates)); read_filter_radio_states walks the scene for `state.<i>` and `focused_index`. TodoMvcView::update reducer matches the dotted intent_tag!("todo_filter", "selected") wire form and writes the new FilterMode into the shared Rc<Signal<FilterMode>>. apply_key_filter implements W3C ARIA roving-tabindex: ArrowLeft/Right cycle, Home/End jump, Space/Enter activate; focusable_tags now [TF_TAG, FILTER_TAG]; access_focus_target returns AccessFocus::composite with active-descendant per R51.87 + R51.66.

examples/todomvc/src/main.rs: build_filter_row extended with per-radio M3 state-layer overlay (Hover=lerp 0.08 OnSurface; Pressed=lerp 0.12; Disabled/Idle untouched). access_node per-segment AccessState now carries live hovered/pressed/disabled bits derived from the same FilterRadioStates snapshot. R659 r659_filter_external_* test block (~130 LOC) replaced with R660 V::update reducer unit tests (intent dispatch by wire-form tag, out-of-range silent no-op, unrelated-tag isolation).

crates/pinion-core/src/widgets/scrollbar.rs: ScrollBarInteractionSignal (Signal<u8> wrapper around ScrollBarState; numeric tag bypasses Forge-generated enum's missing Serialize/DeserializeOwned bound) + use_scrollbar_interaction(tag) Owner::cache hook ([[owner-cache-typed-key]] pattern, mirrors use_text_edit_state). ScrollBar.interaction field + ScrollBar::attach_interaction builder; ScrollBarExternal::attach_interaction delegates via std::mem::take. ScrollBar::send mirrors post-transition state into the signal so view-fn paints repaint on every SCXML state-machine edge.

crates/pinion-widget-paint/src/scrollbar.rs: view_vertical_scrollbar gains 4th arg `interaction: ScrollBarState`. thumb_fill_for_state composes M3 thumb state-layer (Idle=Outline; Hover=lerp 0.08 OnSurface; Dragging=lerp 0.16 OnSurface; Disabled=lerp 0.62 toward SurfaceContainerHighest) via Color::lerp linear-space ([[color-lerp-linear-space]]). R660 unit tests pin 4-state tint distinctness across light + dark palettes + use_scrollbar_interaction shared-handle contract.

examples/hello-listbox/src/main.rs + examples/todomvc/src/main.rs: both consumers thread the new use_scrollbar_interaction hook through view_vertical_scrollbar (`.get()` auto-subscribe) and create_extra_externals (`.attach_interaction(...)` builder) so hover/drag on the scrollbar thumb repaints in lock-step across the substrate.

crates/pinion-rpc/src/dispatch.rs + crates/pinion-shell/src/substrate.rs: DeferredInput::Drag variant + scene/drag RPC method (mutually-exclusive from/from_path and to/to_path endpoint selectors; steps default 8). Shell drain expands Drag into cursor_moved(from) + mouse_pressed + N interpolated cursor_moved + mouse_released so the InputRouter capture lock + receiving widget's pointer_move arc fires identically to a real-mouse drag.
tools/rpc_verify.py: drag() Python wrapper around scene/drag matching the existing click/wheel/key shape (path or coordinate selectors; non-negative steps).

crates/pinion-core/src/widgets/radio_group.rs + crates/pinion-core/src/widgets/listbox.rs: invoke("send") arm migrated from inline `s.split_once(':')` to crate::composite_tag::parse_send_payload. 5-of-5 substrate maturity (TodoDelete + Toggle + Filter framework composite + RadioGroup + ListBox); composite_tag module doc updated to reflect the Rule-of-Three carry repaid.

tools/demos/todomvc_r660.py: 40-assertion end-to-end demo. Covers paint-side filter click (Option β walk-back wire), composite-tag mutual exclusion across the three segments, keyboard cycle (ArrowLeft/Right/Home/End/Space with focus pinned via focus/set on FILTER_TAG), scrollbar drag via the new scene/drag harness (thumb-y delta confirms ScrollBarExternal::pointer_move wrote ScrollState::scroll_to), R655/R656/R657/R658/R659 carry contract regression sweep.
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace passes — 3303 tests across the workspace, 0 failed (todomvc 67/67, hello-listbox 16/16, pinion-widget-paint 23/23 incl. 6 new R660 thumb-state tests, pinion-core 1285/1285 incl. composite_tag 5-of-5 lift regression, pinion-rpc 734/734, pinion-shell 241/241).
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello passes with the workspace.lints baseline (forbid unsafe / deny clippy::pedantic) — no warnings.
tools/demos/todomvc_r660.py PASS in 6.57s with 40 assertions; AI-first introspection contract (§2 #2) cleared with new scene/drag axis the prior wheel-only test cover could not reach.

manual visual: cargo run -p todomvc — filter buttons respond to Tab + Arrow Left/Right + Home/End + Space; scrollbar thumb shifts colour on hover (lerp 0.08 OnSurface) and during drag (lerp 0.16 OnSurface); paint-side filter click still drives selection through the new RadioGroupExternal substrate.
hello-listbox visual regression check — same scrollbar M3 state-layer (substrate 2nd consumer) without any binding-side changes beyond the create_extra_externals interaction-mirror wire.
carry_forward_bullets: LOC overshoot honest: net ~+800 LOC across the round vs the seed-prompt target of net-negative (substrate-heavy round; the R660-5 doc-compression pass on todomvc/src/main.rs deferred to R661 carry rather than churned alongside the substantial substrate changes — risk-reward call). Process-maturity carry: a future round dedicated to doc compression (no behaviour change) lands the negative-LOC ratio when the surface is stable.

scene/invoke + scene/query v0 primary-only — the new scene/drag inherits the same limitation: it dispatches through the InputRouter under the capture lock so it reaches every External (primary + extra) implicitly, but direct introspect on ExtraExternals (e.g. /external/todo_filter/state.0) still 404s. R690+ path-syntax axis carries this.

TUI parity — RadioGroupExternal + new scene/drag substrate are GUI-tested only this round. The TUI backend supports the introspect surface but a TUI-side R660 verify (focusable_tags + apply_key parity, drag has no TUI analogue) is a deliberate carry until the §6 #6 TUI parity cascade gets its own debt-clearance round.

Filter group AT navigation — AT-side `Focus` action on a specific filter segment (driving RadioGroup::set_focused_index without activation) reaches the framework via the existing access_child_invoke channel hello-radio-group covers, but the todomvc binding does not override that hook yet — the AT-only divergence path is a carry. Most AT clients drive `Click`/`Default` which already lands on the standard composite-tag wire here.

ScrollBarInteractionSignal numeric-tag indirection (Signal<u8> wrapper around the Forge-generated `ScrollBarState`) is a stop-gap for the missing Serialize/Deserialize derives on codegen-emitted enums. A future Forge round that lands canonical serde derives on every SCXML-produced state enum lets the wrapper retire — substrate carry, not a binding bug.

The textbook canonical evaluation tracks user-facing concerns (kbd nav, a11y) as part of substrate ROI rather than premature optimisation.

crates/pinion-shell/src/substrate.rs: deferred-input drain arm expands DoubleClick into cursor_moved(MOUSE, x, y) + 2x (mouse_pressed + mouse_released). Framework-first ([[r47-class-incident-prevention]]): double-click is industry-precedent input primitive (W3C UIEvent.detail:2, winit MouseInput chain, every desktop toolkit since Smalltalk-80). Lifting it as a substrate before R664 application consumer (todomvc edit-in-place) lands keeps the application-tier strictly substrate-consuming.

winit-side double-click detection (300ms / 5px threshold) — currently the substrate fires DoubleClick only when the AI client explicitly requests scene/double_click. R664.decision_summary: R664 §5.16 §5.38 §5.39 §5.49 — todomvc edit-in-place + R663 paint-side double-click substrate consumer + focus_request mailbox + AT-action coverage
changes_bullets: pinion-runtime::input::InputRouter — W3C native paint-side double-click detection (300ms / 5px threshold per axis, same target gate). Second consecutive pointer_down on the same hover_target within the window dispatches a synthetic `DoubleClick` named event in addition to `PointerDown`. Unifies the R663 RPC DeferredInput::DoubleClick drain (zero-delta drain trivially fires detection) with native winit MouseInput presses at the framework tier per [[r47-class-incident-prevention]]. 4 unit tests pin the threshold matrix (back-to-back / spatial / cross-target / triple-press reset).

pinion-core::focus_request — programmatic focus-change mailbox (`request(tag)` / `drain()`, thread_local Cell<Option<String>> last-write-wins). New module so widget bodies (External::invoke, reducers, Effect callbacks) can request focus without reaching across the pinion-runtime FocusManager boundary. Mirrors React useImperativeHandle / Solid createRef / Flutter FocusNode.requestFocus shape. 5 unit tests cover the request/drain/clear/overwrite/owned-payload contract.

pinion-shell::ShellCore::handle_tail — drain_focus_request post-dispatch hook applies pending focus requests through FocusManager::focus_set + notify_focus_change so External::on_focus_change observers fire identically to a mouse-driven focus transition. Substrate-side, no application surface change.

examples/todomvc — edit-in-place axis lands end-to-end: use_editing_id reactive Signal<Option<u64>>, TodoEditExternal (5th ExtraExternal under ITEM_TAG) handling `<id>:DoubleClick` via composite-tag wire, TextFieldExternal at EDIT_TF_TAG (6th ExtraExternal) wired through use_text_edit_state/use_caret_blink/use_clipboard, build_todos_list conditional row swap to tf_paint::view_field (3rd consumer of the R657-lifted substrate — view_field ROI confirmed), apply_key_edit handler (Enter commit / Escape cancel / delegate other), commit_edit erase-to-delete (TasteJS canonical), strikethrough TextDecoration on completed item text (2nd consumer of pinion-core TextDecoration substrate). State tuple expanded to (TextFieldState, u32, FilterRadioStates, TextFieldState, u32) to carry editor SCXML state + caret. Multi-text-input apply_composition / apply_middle_click extended for EDIT_TF_TAG target.

examples/todomvc::WidgetA11y::access_child_invoke — extended for 4 composites via per_item_int_action helper (delete / toggle / item-edit) + filter_at_action split. R662 parent_tag substrate reaches 4-of-4 application consumer push (filter / delete / toggle / item). AT-side Click on todo_item enters edit mode (the AT equivalent of double-click).

tools/demos/todomvc_r664.py — 34-assertion AI-first introspection demo: boot steady state → add 3 rows → double-click activates edit → seed text + auto-focus → Backspace + retype + Enter commit → row text updated → Escape cancel → erase-to-delete → strikethrough decoration on completed row → re-entry editor cleanup → selector validation. Drives entirely through scene/double_click + scene/key + scene/snapshot (primary-External-only RPC v0 limit honored via state-snapshot introspect-field walk).

examples/todomvc test battery — 17 new R664 regressions (use_editing_id default / begin_edit activate + stale / view paint swap on/off / commit preserves completed / commit erase-deletes / cancel preserves / focus_request both directions / send DoubleClick wire / send Pointer no-op / focusable_tags / strikethrough decoration / AT Click on item-delete-toggle). Pre-existing tests migrated to 5-tuple State + `r664_create_extra_externals_registers_six_siblings` consolidated count assertion per [[test-name-numeric-count-renaming]].

§1 Vision section — Phase A/B/C/D progression update (Foundation → Professional GUI → Game-engine dual-execution per §2 #4 → AAA editor self-hosted), R663.5 caveats annotating the §2 #4 mode toggle as game-engine entry point rather than GUI diff optimization.
verification_bullets: Workspace: cargo test --workspace = 3328 passed / 0 failed (R663 baseline 3303 + 25 new — 4 InputRouter double-click + 5 focus_request + 17 todomvc R664 - 1 retired duplicate count test).
Workspace: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello = clean (pedantic deny baseline preserved).

Visible: cargo run --release -p todomvc — double-click on row text reveals inline editor with seeded text + caret at end, Enter commits + restores main field focus, Escape cancels untouched, completed row text rendered with strikethrough decoration.
AI-first verify: python3 tools/demos/todomvc_r664.py = PASS in 5.72s (34 assertions covering edit entry + commit + cancel + erase-delete + strikethrough + re-entry cleanup).

InputRouter unit tests cover W3C threshold matrix: back-to-back zero-delay → DoubleClick fires; 10px-apart presses → no DoubleClick; cross-target presses → no DoubleClick; triple press → exactly 2 DoubleClick across 4 presses (binary single/double per [[abstraction-needs-second-consumer]] until a triple consumer surfaces).

focus_request mailbox unit tests pin the request → drain → clear → overwrite contract; owned-String payload accepted for future dynamic-key consumer; thread_local Cell::take pattern preserves zero-cost steady state.
carry_forward_bullets: scene/query + scene/invoke v0 are primary-External-only (R690+ multi-External addressing carry) — the R664 demo works around via state-scene snapshot introspect-field walk; the R690 lift unifies query/invoke selector with the introspect surface.

scene/double_click at-coord form against Scene::Scroll content uses content-local rect (R51.200 absolute_rect_of carry) — R664 demo skips at-form on rows inside the scroll viewport, uses path-form which the substrate routes correctly.

EDIT_TF_TAG is unconditionally in focusable_tags so the programmatic focus_request succeeds; Tab order visits a ghost stop when no row is editing. Dynamic focusable_tags (per-paint refresh) is a substrate axis deferred until a 2nd consumer of conditional focus-stops surfaces per [[abstraction-needs-second-consumer]].

Per-item TextEditState multi-instance (dynamic Owner::cache key) deferred — single-slot reuse satisfies TasteJS canonical (one row editable at a time). Lift when a 2nd consumer of multi-row simultaneous edit surfaces.
SCE-004 (vendor/sce Forge codegen serde derive) honest carry — external dependency, R664 cannot land directly.

R665.decision_summary: R665 §3 §5.15 — Storage substrate + pinion-platform-storage FileStorage + todomvc External(opaque) persistence cycle (Phase A advance 70%→~80%)
changes_bullets: pinion-core::storage — new module. `Storage` trait (load/save/remove, total surface, bytes-only) + `InMemoryStorage` default impl (`RefCell<BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>>`). Mirror of `Clipboard` / `InMemoryClipboard` (R56.1.e §5.22) substrate-shape: trait + headless default in pinion-core, platform impl in a sibling crate. Re-exported through pinion_core::lib root (`Storage`, `InMemoryStorage`). 9 unit tests cover fresh-default / round-trip / overwrite / empty-bytes / remove / multi-key isolation / dyn polymorphism / binary payloads.

pinion-platform-storage — new workspace crate (16th). `FileStorage::try_new(root)` opens a per-app directory (idempotent `create_dir_all`); `Storage` impl writes via tempfile + flush + sync_all + atomic rename so POSIX `rename(2)` / Windows `MoveFileEx(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)` covers the whole transaction (no torn half-writes). Strict key sanitization (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]` 1..=200) so the on-disk filename is a verbatim copy of the key — portable across OSes without escape encoding. `open_app_storage(name)` convenience wrapper composes `dirs::data_dir()` + `try_new` (Linux `$XDG_DATA_HOME/<name>/`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/<name>/`, Windows `%APPDATA%\<name>\`). 15 unit tests cover round-trip / reopen persistence / atomic-write-no-leftover-tmp / list_keys exclude tempfiles / invalid-key rejection (traversal + separators + null + non-ASCII + whitespace + empty + oversize) / key validator + path helpers / dyn polymorphism / default_app_dir / open_app_storage end-to-end.

examples/todomvc — first consumer of the §3 External(opaque) escape hatch as persistence. `PersistedState { schema_version: u32, todos: Vec<TodoItem>, filter: FilterMode, next_id: u64 }` single-blob shape (atomic-write covers the whole transaction). `use_storage()` Owner::cache hook with `AppStorage(Box<dyn Storage>)` sized newtype (mirror of `AppClipboard`). `use_persistence_boot()` runs ONCE per Owner: (1) pre-resolves all dependent `Owner::cache` slots BEFORE entering the boot slot factory to avoid nested `RefCell::borrow_mut` panic; (2) loads `todomvc.state` from disk + deserializes via serde_json + schema-version-checks + seeds Signals via `pinion_core::reactive::batch`; (3) installs a save `Effect` retained in `PersistenceBootMarker { _save_effect: Effect }` — Effect's Rc<EffectInner> must be held because Owner cleanup queue stores only Weak (R37.5 #2 leak fix), dropping the handle silently GCs the Effect. `PINION_STORAGE_DIR` env var override path for test isolation; default = `pinion-todomvc` app dir. Fallback chain: env-override → app-dir → `InMemoryStorage` (headless CI / sandboxed containers wire up unchanged).
examples/todomvc::Cargo.toml — new dep `pinion-platform-storage`. Workspace Cargo.toml gains `crates/pinion-platform-storage` member entry; transitive `dirs = 5` cargo dep.

Effect handle retention bug fixed inline: Owner::cleanup queue stores Weak<EffectInner> (R37.5 #2 leak fix), so the Effect handle returned from `Effect::new(&owner, ...)` MUST be held by the application — dropping it silently GCs the EffectInner and Signal subscriber lists' `Weak<dyn ReactiveNode>` becomes dangling, killing save fires. Nested Owner::cache panic fixed inline: Owner::cache holds `RefCell::borrow_mut` on its inner HashMap for the factory closure's duration; nested `Owner::cache` calls (use_storage / use_todos / etc. inside the boot factory) would re-enter `borrow_mut` and panic. Pre-resolution pattern: all dependent slots resolved BEFORE entering the outer boot slot factory. Generalizable substrate constraint, candidate new memory entry [[owner-cache-no-nested-factory]].

R51.150 future driver hooks?) faces the same Weak-vs-Strong owner cleanup queue trap. 2nd consumer would trigger lift to a `framework::OwnedEffect` helper that internalizes the retention discipline.

next_id Cell non-reactive read inside Effect — works because `allocate_todo_id` mutates Cell BEFORE the `todos.set_with` that fires the Effect subscription. Defensive guard: convert `use_next_todo_id` to `Signal<u64>` once a 2nd writer surfaces.

Type changes / field removal bump `PERSISTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` and the load path falls through to defaults (current behaviour — no real migrator). A proper migrator with field-mapping table lands when the first breaking-change axis demands it (YAGNI honest).

R670.B.decision_summary: R670.B — Phase B (R700+) first real dogfood. AppShell multi-window refactor (per-WindowSlot cluster lift + per-window winit/accesskit/IME/intrinsic-resize dispatch) + RPC {window: "<id>"} param + WidgetView::view_for_window per-window paint hook + examples/hello-multi-window first multi-window consumer (main Button + inspector state-debug Text mirror via shared ShellCore).
